items.title: AWS services in one line
items.body:
EC2: virtual machines            Lambda: run code without servers
ECS/EKS: containers / Kubernetes  S3: object storage
EBS: block disks for EC2          EFS: shared file system
RDS: managed SQL databases        DynamoDB: managed NoSQL key-value
VPC: your private network         Route 53: DNS
CloudFront: CDN                   ELB: load balancers

items.title: AWS services in one line (platform)
items.body:
IAM: users, roles and permissions     KMS: encryption keys
Secrets Manager: store secrets         CloudWatch: metrics, logs, alarms
SQS: message queue                     SNS: pub/sub notifications
CloudFormation / CDK: infrastructure as code
ECR: container image registry          CloudTrail: audit log of API calls

items.title: IAM least-privilege principles
items.body:
- Never use the root account for daily work; enable MFA on it
- Prefer roles (temporary credentials) over long-lived access keys
- Grant specific actions on specific resources, not "*"
- Use groups/roles for people, separate roles for applications
- Review unused permissions (IAM Access Analyzer, last-used data)
- Rotate or delete old access keys; never commit keys to git
items.description: Give only the access that is needed.

items.title: IAM policy: read-only on one S3 bucket
Regions and Availability Zones
items.body:
Region: a geographic area (eu-west-1 Ireland, us-east-1 N. Virginia); data stays there unless you move it.
Availability Zone (AZ): one or more data centres inside a region (eu-west-1a, 1b, 1c).
Design for high availability: spread across at least two AZs.
Pick a region by latency to users, legal/data-residency rules, service availability and price.

items.title: Cloud cost-safety checklist
items.body:
[ ] Set a monthly budget with email alerts (AWS Budgets) and enable billing alarms
[ ] Enable MFA on the root account and do not create root access keys
[ ] Stop or terminate instances you are not using
[ ] Delete unattached EBS volumes, old snapshots and unused Elastic IPs
[ ] Watch NAT Gateways and data transfer; they cost money while idle
[ ] Empty and delete test S3 buckets; set lifecycle rules
[ ] Tag resources with project and owner so you can find what to delete
[ ] Check the free-tier limits and expiry dates
[ ] Use smaller instance types and auto-shutdown schedules for dev
[ ] Review Cost Explorer weekly while learning

items.title: Cloud security basics checklist
items.body:
[ ] No public S3 buckets unless intended (Block Public Access on)
[ ] Security groups open only the ports you need, never 0.0.0.0/0 for SSH or databases
[ ] Databases are in private subnets
[ ] Secrets are in Secrets Manager or Parameter Store, not in code
[ ] Encryption at rest and in transit is on
[ ] CloudTrail is enabled
[ ] Backups exist and a restore has been tested

items.title: Shared responsibility model
items.body:
Provider is responsible for security OF the cloud: hardware, data centres, the hypervisor, managed-service internals.
You are responsible for security IN the cloud: identities and permissions, data, guest OS patching (on VMs), network rules, application code, configuration.

items.title: IaaS vs PaaS vs SaaS
items.body:
IaaS (EC2, VMs): you manage OS, runtime, app; provider manages hardware.
PaaS (Elastic Beanstalk, App Service, Heroku): you manage the app and data.
SaaS (Gmail, Slack): provider manages everything; you configure and use it.
Serverless (Lambda): you supply functions; pay per execution.

items.title: Scaling terms
items.body:
Vertical scaling: a bigger machine (more CPU/RAM). Simple, has a ceiling.
Horizontal scaling: more machines behind a load balancer. Needs stateless apps.
Elasticity: scale out and in automatically with demand (Auto Scaling).
High availability: no single point of failure (multi-AZ).

items.title: SSH into an EC2 instance
items.body:

ssh -i {{key_name}}.pem ec2-user@{{public_ip}}      # Amazon Linux; Ubuntu AMIs use ubuntu@

items.title: Docker image to a registry (ECR)
items.body:
aws ecr get-login-password --region {{region}} | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin {{account_id}}.dkr.ecr.{{region}}.amazonaws.com
docker tag {{image}}:latest {{account_id}}.dkr.ecr.{{region}}.amazonaws.com/{{image}}:latest
docker push {{account_id}}.dkr.ecr.{{region}}.amazonaws.com/{{image}}:latest

items.title: Free-tier friendly learning tips
items.body:
- Use a separate learning account; never put real customer data in it
- Prefer t3.micro / t2.micro instances and the smallest database sizes
- Destroy what you create when the lab ends (terraform destroy / delete the stack)
- Name resources with a lab prefix to find leftovers quickly
